key_insight: In a supersonic reacting shear layer, finite-time stretching structures organize transport and strongly align with scalar-gradient enrichment in the mid-plane.
engineering_relevance: These coherent transport skeletons help explain and potentially control mixing, combustion, and scalar-transport behavior in high-speed reacting flows.
method: Computed forward/backward FTLE fields from time-resolved mid-plane DNS data.
Extracted FTLE-ridge skeletons and quantified ridge overlap, persistence, and scalar-conditioned transport.
Reconstructed Cauchy-Green deformation tensors to extract hyperbolic geodesic LCS as strainlines seeded at high-λmax locations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports localized forward/backward ridge overlap, strong scalar-gradient enrichment, finite-time geodesic LCS on the same high-strain skeleton, and compact scalar-response lags relative to decorrelation and FTLE-integration scales.
watch_item: Because the analysis is based on a constrained 2D slice of a 3D compressible reacting flow, ridge and LCS interpretations may depend on plane selection and finite-time window choices.
paper_title: Planar Lagrangian transport and scalar-gradient organization in a turbulent reacting shear layer
